'''Boris Borisovich Kadomtsev''' ({{langx|ru|Борис Борисович Кадомцев}}; 9 November 1928 – 19 August 1998) was a Soviet and Russian [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physicist]] who worked on controlled fusion problems (e.g. [[tokamak]]s).<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kadomtsev|first=B. B.|date=1991|title=Plasma transport in tokamaks|journal=Nuclear Fusion|language=en|volume=31|issue=7|pages=1301–1314|doi=10.1088/0029-5515/31/7/006|s2cid=120120016 |issn=0029-5515}}</ref> He developed a theory of transport phenomena in turbulent plasmas and a theory of the so-called anomalous behavior of plasmas in magnetic fields.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kadomtsev|first=B. B.|date=1987|title=Plasma magnetic insulation|journal=Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series A, Mathematical and Physical Sciences|volume=322|issue=1563|pages=125–131|doi=10.1098/rsta.1987.0042|bibcode=1987RSPTA.322..125K|s2cid=120560639}}</ref> In 1966, he discovered plasma instability with trapped particles.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kadomtsev|first=B. B.|date=1966|title=Hydromagnetic Stability of a Plasma|url=https://courses.physics.ucsd.edu/2012/Winter/physics218b/SuppRead%20Kadomtsev.pdf|journal=Reviews of Plasma Physics|volume=2|pages=153–199|bibcode=1966RvPP....2..153K}}</ref>

In 1970, Kadomtsev and [[Vladimir Petviashvili]] introduced into plasma physics the [[Kadomtsev–Petviashvili equation]] (KP equation), a nonlinear partial differential equation with applications in [[theoretical physics]] and [[complex analysis]]. The exact solution to the KP equation was later found by [[Vladimir E. Zakharov|Vladimir Zakharov]] and {{ill|Alexei Shabat|de|Alexei Borissowitsch Schabat}}, which helped solve the [[Schottky problem]].<ref>{{Citation|last=Mulase|first=Motohico|title=Algebraic Analysis|chapter=KP Equations, Strings, and the Schottky Problem|date=1988|chapter-url=http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/B9780124004665500081|pages=473–492|editor-last=Kashiwara|editor-first=Masaki|publisher=Academic Press|language=en|doi=10.1016/b978-0-12-400466-5.50008-1|isbn=978-0-12-400466-5|access-date=2020-03-08|editor2-last=Kawai|editor2-first=Takahiro}}</ref>

== Early life and career ==
Kadomtsev graduated from [[Moscow State University]] in 1951. He then worked at the Institute for Physics and Energy in [[Obninsk]]. Starting in 1956, he worked at the Institute for Atomic Energy. From 1976 to 1998, he was the chief editor of the journal ''[[Physics-Uspekhi]]'' ("Successes in Physics")''.''<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Гинзбург|first=Виталий Лазаревич|date=2009|title=К истории журнала "Успехи физических наук" (вступительное слово)|url=https://ufn.ru/ru/articles/2009/6/b/|journal=Успехи физических наук|language=ru|volume=179|issue=6|pages=562–570|issn=0042-1294}}</ref>

From 1973 until his death in 1998, he was the chair of the plasma physics section of the state committee for the use of nuclear energy.

He died on 19 August 1998 and was buried at [[Troyekurovskoye Cemetery]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://moscow-tombs.narod.ru/1998/kadomtsev_bb.htm|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120716221637/http://moscow-tombs.narod.ru/1998/kadomtsev_bb.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=2012-07-16|title=Московские могилы. Кадомцев Б.Б.|date=2012-07-16|website=archive.is|access-date=2020-03-08}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
In 1970, he received the [[USSR State Prize]] for the study of the instability of a high-temperature plasma in a magnetic field and the creation of a method for its stabilization with a “magnetic well”.

In 1984, he was awarded the [[Lenin Prize]] for his work on the "''Theory of Thermonuclear Toroidal Plasma''".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.osti.gov/etdeweb/biblio/5976508|title=Theory of thermonuclear toroidal plasma (Journal Article) {{!}} ETDEWEB|website=www.osti.gov|access-date=2020-03-08}}</ref>

He was also honored with the [[Order of the Red Banner of Labour]]. He has been a corresponding member of the Soviet Academy of Sciences since 1962 and a full member since 1970.

In 1998, he received the [[American Physical Society]]'s [[James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics]] for "''fundamental contributions to plasma turbulence theory, stability and nonlinear theory of [[Magnetohydrodynamics|MHD]] and kinetic instabilities in plasmas, and for international leadership in research and teaching of plasma physics and [[Fusion power|controlled thermonuclear fusion]] physics"''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Kadomtsev&first_nm=Boris&year=1998|title=1998 James Clerk Maxwell Prize for Plasma Physics Recipient|website=American Physical Society|language=en|access-date=2020-03-08}}</ref>
